conflicts.description: Which of the two lower pop bumpers is switch 31, coil Q10 and lamp 61, and which is switch 32, Q11 and lamp 62. The ROM's switch, coil and lamp tests name 31, Q10 and 61 LEFT POP BUMPER and 32, Q11 and 62 RIGHT POP BUMPER, and the bumper probe shows each switch firing its own coil and lamp. The parts book's bumper page (printed b13, a page whose title, 'Left, Right & Bottom Bumper', is generic) prints 'LAMPS 60 (TOP) 61 (RIGHT) 62 (LEFT)' and the switch callout 'TOP / RIGHT / LEFT' beside 'SW. 30 / SW. 31 / SW. 32'. The retained table agrees with the ROM on the lamps (l61a on the left bumper, l62a on the right) but places its bumper objects as the parts book does (sw31 on the right, sw32 on the left) and plays its LeftJet sound on sw31. A recreation needs to know which side each address is. The definition labels and places them by the ROM's names. Resolution path: close the left lower pop bumper's switch on a physical NBA in switch test and read the number the display prints, or find Stern's NBA switch and lamp location drawings; an owner could settle it in a minute.

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest in the trough assembly 500-6318-24-ND on micro switches 18, 19 and 20 and on the beam of the dual opto boards at position 21, the right-hand end where the up-kicker sits (the ROM names 18 TROUGH #4 (L) and 21 TROUGH #1 (R)). Q1 (26-1200) lifts the right-most ball past the jam beam 22 into the shooter lane, where it rests on switch 23 (shooter lane switch 180-5157-00). The player plunges it with the ball shooter assembly, or the autoplunger Q2 (24-940) fires it. In the retained gameplay probes the ROM pulsed Q1 at Start and did not fire Q2 for the first ball while switch 23 was closed. Keep per-position occupancy rather than a count.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough, shooter lane and autoplunger

mechanisms.behavior: An eject hole: a ball closes switch 35 and Q4 kicks it out. In the retained gameplay probe the ROM pulsed Q4 and energized the basket magnet Q3 while switch 35 was closed, which agrees with IPDB's trajectory up-kicker that sends the ball airborne towards the hoop; the retained table models this hole as that kicker (a 55-degree kick towards the Magna-hoop). The parts book lists a 40-degree long-throw kicker 500-7157-01 (27-1400 coil) and a 30-degree eject 500-6511-01-ND (24-940 coil) without saying which hole each one serves.
mechanisms.label: Left eject (switch 35, Q4)

mechanisms.behavior: An eject hole: a ball closes switch 9 and Q20 kicks it out. In the retained gameplay probe the ROM pulsed Q20 while switch 9 was closed and flashed Q19, Q27 and Q31. The retained table kicks it out flat.
mechanisms.label: Right eject (switch 9, Q20)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets M, V, P, from the rear: (M)VP switch 13, M(V)P 12 and MV(P) 11, each on its own interrupter of the slotted opto PCB 520-5252-03. A target's switch reads closed while it is down; Q7 (24-940) raises the whole bank. Lamps 57-59 spell the same letters. In the retained gameplay probe the ROM fired Q7 and the shaker Q8 after the third target went down and kept pulsing Q7 for as long as the switches still read down.
mechanisms.label: M-V-P 3-bank drop target

mechanisms.behavior: The Magna-hoop assembly 500-7162-00 carries a magnet and connector assembly 511-5221-00 behind its backboard plastic (IPDB photo: 'Electromagnet Behind Hoop Backboard'); basket opto 34 sees a ball pass through the hoop. The ROM energized Q3 with the left eject Q4 in the retained gameplay probe. How long the magnet holds a ball and what releases it are not documented; the retained table holds the ball at the backboard until it reaches switch 34.
mechanisms.label: Magna-hoop basket magnet

mechanisms.behavior: The ROM names Q5 RAMP DIVERTER. The parts book lists one diverter assembly 515-6596-00-A9 on the left plastic ramp 500-7158-00, and IPDB's designer note mentions a wire ramp / divert mechanism. Which ramp exits its positions select is not documented; the retained table swaps two walls on the left side of the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Ramp diverter (Q5)

mechanisms.behavior: The ROM names Q12 BASKET DIVERTER. IPDB's designer note mentions a lift flap assembly in the plastic ramp (the ramp-on-a-ramp that sends a fast ball airborne towards the hoop), and the parts book lists an up-post assembly 500-7161-00 titled 'LIFT RAMP' with a 26-1200 coil; neither ties a coil number to them. The retained table rotates a flap into the ball's path near the top centre while Q12 is energized.
mechanisms.label: Basket diverter (Q12)

mechanisms.behavior: The ROM names Q21 ORBIT UP/DOWN POST and drives it as a held output: in the retained probes it changes state once at a time (after the ball leaves the shooter lane, after a flipper press, at the first pop-bumper hit). The retained table raises a post across the orbit while Q21 is energized. The physical post assembly is not identified in the partial parts book.
mechanisms.label: Orbit up/down post (Q21)

mechanisms.behavior: A motorized disk in the centre of the playfield: spinning disk assembly 500-7144-01 with motor 511-5190-00 and disk/hub weldment 515-7714-00 under an adhesive art pad. Q6 is the motor and Q22 the SPINNING DISK MOTOR RELAY: the ROM's coil test energizes Q22 together with Q6 and Q22 alone, and in the retained bumper probe the ROM switched Q6 and Q22 on and off together. What the relay switches (for example motor direction or supply) is not documented, so the disk's direction and speed control are unknown.
mechanisms.label: Spinning disk

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB lists one captive ball; switch 10 (CAPTIVE BALL) reports a hit and flash Q30 and lamp 22 (captive ball arrow) belong to it. The retained table models a captive ball striking a target in the upper left.
mechanisms.label: Captive ball

mechanisms.behavior: Three pop bumpers with 26-1200 coils Q9-Q11, stack switches 180-5015-04 and white wedge-base LED modules. The retained probe pairs switch 30 with Q9 and lamp 60 (TOP), 31 with Q10 and lamp 61 and 32 with Q11 and lamp 62; every hit also runs the shaker Q8 and flashes Q31. The ROM names 31/Q10/61 LEFT and 32/Q11/62 RIGHT, the parts book the reverse (conflict.pop-bumper-sides).
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left slingshot Q17 with switch 26 and right slingshot Q18 with switch 27 (23-800 coils, assembly 500-5849-00-ND with two stack switches 180-5054-00 each). The retained probe shows each switch firing its own coil and the slingshot flash Q32.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Q15 (23-1500) drives the left flipper assembly 500-6543-15-ND and Q16 (23-900) the right assembly 500-6543-05-ND, each with a power (EOS) switch 180-5149-00 on dedicated D-10 / D-12. The cabinet buttons are single-stack switches on D-9 / D-11; no upper flipper is fitted. In the retained gameplay probe each held button made the ROM energize its own flipper coil.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: The remaining playfield switches at their enumerated addresses: the left 4-bank (1-4, rear to front) and right 3-bank (5-7) stand-up targets, the pop-bumper target 47, the left and right orbits (14, 36), the right ramp entrance and exit (8, 37), the left ramp entrance (33), and the outlanes and return lanes (24, 25, 28, 29). Use the pulse flag recorded on each switch; the parts book lists ramp opto transceivers and roll-under switches without addresses.
mechanisms.label: Lanes, orbits, ramps and stand-up targets

mechanisms.behavior: The ROM names Q8 SHAKER MOTOR (OPTIONAL) and drives it on every pop-bumper hit and the MVP bank reset in the retained probes; the parts book lists no shaker. Q24 OPTIONAL COIL is skipped by the coil test but pulsed for about 130 ms once per coin in the retained runs, as a coin meter or knocker would be; the parts book lists an optional +12 V meter that was not included with this machine.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker motor and optional coil

physical.notes: The ROM's Single Coil Test shows "TROUGH UP-KICKER" with the wire colours YEL-VIO / BRN-BLK and fires public solenoid 1. The parts book's trough page prints the coil as Q1. It lifts the right-most trough ball past the jam opto 22 into the shooter lane. Spatial: the table's BallRelease kicker at the trough exit; the up-kicker coil is below the playfield.

The ROM's Single Coil Test shows "AUTO LAUNCH" with the wire colours YEL-VIO / BRN-RED and fires public solenoid 2. Autoplunger coil (parts book Q2) that fires the ball resting on shooter-lane switch 23. Spatial: shares the shooter-lane trigger point; the table's autoplunger has no object of its own.

The magnet and connector assembly of the Magna-hoop assembly 500-7162-00 behind the basket's backboard plastic. Spatial: the table's magtrigger, where its basket magnet catches the ball; the magnet is behind the basket's backboard.

The ROM's Single Coil Test shows "LEFT EJECT" with the wire colours YEL-VIO / BRN-YEL and fires public solenoid 4. Kicks the ball out of the left eject (switch 35). The parts book carries a 40-degree long-throw kicker 500-7157-01 (27-1400 coil) and a 30-degree eject 500-6511-01-ND (24-940 coil) without saying which eject each one is. Spatial: the left eject hole (the table's kicker object named "shooter").

The ROM's Single Coil Test shows "RAMP DIVERTER" with the wire colours YEL-VIO / BRN-GRN and fires public solenoid 5. The parts book lists one diverter assembly (515-6596-00-A9) on the left plastic ramp; whether it is this diverter or the basket diverter Q12 is not printed. Spatial: the mean of the table's two diverter walls div1 and div2, which the script raises and drops in turn; the diverter coil is not modelled.

The ROM's Single Coil Test shows "SPINNING DISK MOTOR" with the wire colours BRN / BRN-BLU and fires public solenoid 6 and 22. Motor of the spinning disk assembly 500-7144-01 (disk/hub weldment 515-7714-00 under an adhesive art pad) in the centre of the playfield. The ROM's coil test energizes public 22 (the motor relay) together with it. Spatial: the centre of the table's spinning-disk turntable trigger (its WheelP disk primitive is at the same point).

The retained probes show the ROM driving it on every pop-bumper hit and on the MVP bank reset, so a fitted shaker runs then.

PinMAME's synthetic S.A.M. game-on state, not a driver-board transistor. sam.c's VBLANK handler reads game RAM at samlocals.fastflipaddr (0x010609be, set for nba_802 only) and publishes public solenoid 33 while that value is 1; nba_500, nba_600, nba_700 and nba_801 have no fast-flip address, so on them it stays 0. A retained diagnostic run of the gameplay probe on nba_802 read that RAM word and PinmameGetSolenoid(33) after every output poll: both turn on about 40 ms after Start and stay on through play (fast-flip diagnostic excerpt). The pinned LibPinMAME build never reports public 33 through its OnSolenoidUpdated callback, though, so the harness traces record no event for it (the same build reports none for Family Guy, whose older-build trace does); a consumer that only listens for solenoid callbacks never receives it, and one that polls the solenoid state does. The retained table runs core sam.vbs fast flips (InitVpmFFlipsSAM), which bind SolCallback(33) to switch flipper control between the ROM's Q15/Q16 and direct button flips.
